question: Why is this case short, and which resource is the bottleneck?
answer:
**Why it's short (CASE-000004, RUN-1688E1B44C11)**

- **Cause:** a resource-competition / shared-machine conflict on supplier SUP-000295, lane LANE-000082, for PART-000030. The disruption runs 2026-11-23 to 2026-11-30 (2 weeks) with a 20% capacity loss and a 14-day lead-time extension. It's confirmed, with 0.95 event confidence.
- **Scope:** two lines are in scope. PART-000030 (LANE-000082) has 600 units of demand and 0 usable stock. PART-000054 (LANE-000136) has 400 units of demand and 0 usable stock, with 200 units offered on its alternate lane.
- **Shortage picture:** PART-000030 already goes short in week 2026-11-02 in both the baseline and disrupted views, with peak backlog 911 baseline vs 922 disrupted. PART-000054 goes short from 2026-11-09 in both, with peak backlog 237 in each.

**Bottleneck**

The tool results don't name a single bottleneck resource. What they do show is that the binding constraint is the shared machine behind LANE-000082 / PART-000030: it's the only line with a capacity loss (20%) and a lead-time extension, and it has no usable stock and no alternate units offered. PART-000054's shortage is essentially unchanged by the disruption (237 vs 237), so it isn't what the disruption is driving.

One caveat: the shortage on PART-000030 starts in 2026-11-02, which is before the disruption window opens on 2026-11-23, and the baseline already shows a 911 peak backlog. So part of the shortfall is pre-existing, not caused by this event.

The existing run RUN-1688E1B44C11 is OPTIMAL and not stale. I can pull its per-mode results or compare modes if you want to see which mitigation covers the gap.
